title: order_direction
description: The Direction stored for an order, its findings, and whether the caller may send a new one

response.description: The order's stored Direction (story-direct's document) and its findings. Only the member who holds the order with a live lease may send a new one; edit_refusal says why not otherwise.

close_reason.description: Why an order stopped or was replaced. A stable code, never free text.

direction_finding.description: A finding on a Direction: story-direct's model-free lint or a Canon cross-check. Warnings.

medium.description: What one work order produces. The medium decides the default lease length.

order_state.description: Where a work order is in its life. issued, directed, rendered and submitted are working states (the assignee owes work and a lease can expire); approved, rejected and abandoned are terminal.

reference_kind.description: What a receipt reference points at: a take made in this ledger (it must name its take_id) or a registered asset approved outside the ledger (it must not).

render_receipt.description: What the server rendered for one work order, signed by the server. A result without a valid receipt is never registered as a take. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of a fixed, per-version list of fields (see fixtures/ledger/receipts.json); fields outside the version's list are not signed, so a later version can add fields without breaking receipts already signed.

version.description: The receipt's own version; it selects the signed field list. Only version 1 can be signed or verified today. Any integer from 1 parses; an unknown version fails verification with receipt_invalid, not parsing.

tenant_id.description: Signed. Binds the receipt to one tenant.

project_id.description: Signed. Binds the receipt to one project.

order_id.description: The work order the render was made for.

member.description: The assignee the receipt was issued to.

canon_revision.description: The approved Canon revision the prompt was rendered against.

direction_kref.description: Reference of the Direction artifact that was rendered.

references.description: The references wired into the render, in slot order.

prompt_sha256.description: Hash of the rendered prompt. Written as the server defines it (the fixtures use a 'sha256:' prefix); the schema does not constrain the form.

profile_id.description: The model profile the prompt was rendered for.

profile_version.description: The version of that profile. A string, not a number.

render_contract_version.description: Version of the render contract the prompt follows.

issued_at.description: Epoch seconds. Must lie within the I-JSON integer range (+-2^53) for the receipt to be signable.

expires_at.description: Epoch seconds; the latest moment the result may be submitted against this receipt.

key_id.description: Id of the signing key. Empty on an unsigned receipt.

signature.description: 'hmac-sha256:' followed by 64 lowercase hex digits. Empty on an unsigned receipt. The form is checked when the signature is verified, not when the document is parsed, so it is not a pattern here.

render_receipt.$comment: Not expressible: a reference of kind take must name its take_id and one of kind asset must not (checked when the receipt is attached to an order, error receipt_invalid); issued_at <= expires_at is not checked by the code either.

render_receipt_reference.description: One reference wired into the render.

slot.description: The slot the reference occupies in the model's addressing scheme.

kref.description: Reference of the take revision or asset.

take_id.description: Required for kind take, null for kind asset (enforced when the receipt is attached).

review_policy.description: How much a person reviews. A work order may override the project's policy.

submission.description: What the host sends back after generating (or writing, for text): where the result is and what produced it.

model_used.description: The model the host actually used. Empty when unknown.

profile_id.description: The model profile the host says it generated with. Empty when it does not know.

final_prompt_sha256.description: Hash of the prompt the host finally sent, if it reworded the rendered one. Empty when unchanged.

work_order.description: One unit of work: making one medium of one Moment. The document is a record; every state change produces a new copy with a higher seq. Times are integer epoch seconds supplied by the caller.

version.description: Ledger record version; 2 today. Any integer from 1 parses, so older stored records stay readable.

seq.description: Bumped by every state change. The storage layer compares and swaps on it.

order_id.description: Also the idempotency key: registering the same result twice yields one take.

scope_id.description: The scene the Moment belongs to. A take awaiting a person holds later orders of the same scope only.

sequence.description: The Moment's place in production order. Reissues keep it.

canon_revision.description: The approved Canon revision the order is pinned to.

depends_on.description: story-core node keys (story_revision_domains, bare kind/id, e.g. character/rhea) this Moment's work leans on, the union over the narrative and production domains. Opaque to the ledger: compared as strings with changed_domains. No entry repeats.

lease_seconds.description: Length of the lease in seconds.

assignee.description: The member the order is bound to; null while unclaimed.

lease_expires_at.description: Epoch seconds the lease ends; null while unclaimed or once the work is done.

anchor.description: A cut later cuts lean on (first appearance, new costume, new location).

policy.description: Per-Moment override of the project's review policy; null means follow the project.

contention_group.description: Orders in one group are deliberate overlaps on the same Moment and medium.

participant.description: In a contention group: the one member this order is for.

profile_id.description: In a contention group: the model profile this order is for, when fixed. On a winner's remake: the profile that won, as a hint.

after_order_ids.description: Anchor orders this one waits on until a person approves their take. Followed through reissues by successor_id.

successor_id.description: The order that replaced this one.

revision_notes.description: The reviewer's notes a remake must address.

direction_revisions.description: Canon revisions the current direction and receipt are valid for. A Canon change that misses depends_on extends this instead of voiding the work.

closed_by.description: The person who approved, rejected, withdrew or superseded. A policy confirmation leaves it null and sets confirmed_by_policy.

work_order.$comment: Not expressible: which fields must be set in which state (assignee and lease_expires_at while working, take_id once recorded, close_reason once closed) is enforced by the transition functions, not by parsing. For every nullable field an absent key and a null mean the same; writers should still emit every field.
